title: an odd dream from childhood; a field with a cedar tree?
content: Has anyone been to a pasture/field with an evergreen tree towards the center, and a small creek around the edge? I was recounting some old dreams of mine, and I remember one taking place in a field where I was having a picnic with my grandmother. It felt incredibly lifelike, and only realized it was a dream when I was older and talking about picnicking, and my grandmother doesn't remember this experience at all. The exact location is my families property, but it felt way bigger, and way more... empty? Like a bizarre version of a place I know better than the back of my hand. We were in the field, setting out a blanket and everything as normal, when I noticed a bee hovering and following me around. I ran back over to my grandmother when I noticed that my grandfather was suddenly with us. I got confused and asked when he got there, because we weren't exactly close to the house, and the only way to get to where we were quickly was via ATV which I didn't hear at all. My grandmother just ignored me, getting the drinks and everything set up so the blanket didn't blow away. That's when I noticed that my grandpa was acting really weird, staring off into the distance, freezing randomly, and staring back towards the path home. I wandered over towards the tree in the middle of the field, and when I turned back, both of my grandparents were staring after me, still as an image. That's when I felt a godawful pain in my hand, and saw a yellow jacket curled up on the back of my hand, stinging the shit out of me. I screamed, ran back towards them, and they just laughed at me, saying that it was fine, it would stop soon, and to eat. I remember drinking something, it tasted like tea I think, but way more floral than I like. It was very light, like almost clear and honey colored. After I had calmed down from the insect sting, I remember noticing something moving from the field across the way; due east from where we were. I don't remember much more than a low to the ground shadow, but my grandparents got extremely cagey and started packing up, and my grandfather went to check it out while I went home with my grandmother. I know we picnicked in that field a lot, but my grandfather NEVER came with us, sitting on the ground was bad for his joints, and he for damn sure wouldn't have walked all the way out there. My grandmother's memory is also really good, she remembers a lot of odd things happening out there, but never laughing at me getting stung, never my grandfather with us, and never going without her dog.
